literal: Like a heron, remain folded at the (unfavorable) time; and then, like its strike, (act) when the opportune time arises.
translation: One should remain inactive like a resting heron when the time is unfavorable, but strike with swift precision like that heron the moment the right opportunity arises.
modern: காலம் சாதகமாக இல்லாதபோது கொக்கைப் போல ஒடுங்கி இருக்க வேண்டும்; காலம் வாய்க்கும்போது அதன் குத்துப்போலத் தப்பாமல் விரைந்து செய்து முடிக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the vivid metaphor of a hunting heron to teach the art of timing. A heron stands perfectly still, folding its wings and appearing completely harmless while waiting for prey. Similarly, a wise person must bide their time patiently and keep a low profile when circumstances are unfavorable. However, the moment the right opportunity presents itself, the heron strikes with lightning speed and absolute precision. In the same way, one must act decisively and without hesitation when the perfect moment arrives.
